correctness.rationale: For the stated two irreducible Metzler generators the positive-duration exponentials and both products are strictly positive. Their equal positive determinant makes the Perron-root comparison exactly a trace comparison. Trace cyclicity and Cayley–Hamilton for the traceless commutator give tr(X²Y²)−tr(XYXY)=det[X,Y]. Exponentials are affine in their generators with positive slope by real spectral interpolation. As an independent root check, for either eigenvalue ℓ of B one can take w=((ℓ+b)/a,1); the eigenvalue sum equation is ℓ(w₁+1)=gw₁. Such a ray is shared exactly at z=b+(1+d/g)ℓ. The smaller eigenvalue is less than −b (the characteristic polynomial takes value −ab at −b) and the larger satisfies 0<λ<g. The commutator determinant is quadratic with leading coefficient −ag, and consequently factors into these two distinct roots, only one positive. This proves strict order with the stated signs for all positive durations. At the positive root both generators preserve the same positive ray, with eigenvalues −dλ/g and λ, so every finite product has the claimed positive Perron multiplier, including the balanced neutrality case. At most three slots with fixed totals can be merged to two by cyclic rotation and the phase semigroup law; at four the two distinct cyclic classes give the strict comparison. The grouped word contains two maximal constant-phase runs, not four physically distinct on-pulses. For large off-time v, scaling both products by exp(−2λv) gives positive rank-one limits X²P and (XP)² with nonzero Perron roots; both growth rates then tend to λ. A common scalar loss chosen strictly between those positive rates yields exactly the asserted opposing multiplier signs relative to one. RESULT.md Proof §§1–4 gives a replay route.
